html:
The map's label for the Lao kingdoms of the middle Mekong from 1650 to 1715. In 1650 they were still one kingdom, Lan Xang, at its height under King Sourigna Vongsa, who reigned from 1638 to about 1695. His long reign was a time of peace, and European visitors, a Dutch merchant and an Italian Jesuit, came to Vientiane in the 1640s.

He left no adult heir, and fights over the throne followed. In 1707 the kingdom split into Vientiane and Luang Phrabang, and in 1713 Champasak broke away in the south. The three small kingdoms were caught between Burma, Siam and Vietnam, and by the late 1700s all were vassals of Siam. The French later joined most of their lands into Laos.
